title: infrastructure-weekly-update-2026-08-31
body:
High level summary:

- Fleet health: Overall GPU availability is stable. Average cluster utilization across hosted pools was 68% for the week (target 60-75%). We saw short spikes in p99 latency tied to a region failover test (details below).
- Capacity: We are on track with the Q3 capacity plan. Remaining procurement for H100 nodes scheduled for delivery mid-September.
- Outages/incidents: One minor regional capacity degradation (EU-west) on 2026-08-28 during a planned rolling upgrade; no customer-facing SLA breaches.
- Priorities next week: finalize H100 rollout playbook, complete node-image upgrade for autoscaling groups, and run a cross-region load test for Dedicated customers.

1) Fleet and capacity metrics (hosted + dedicated combined approximate):
- GPU inventory (logical GPU devices): A100-80GB: 280; H100-80GB: 96; L40: 48.
- Provisioned hosts (baremetal / cloud instances): 140 (mix of p4/p5 and G5 instances across clouds).
- Average utilization (aggregate): 68% (7-day avg).
- Peak demand day (2026-08-27): 92% utilization during a big internal benchmark run.
- Available spare capacity buffer (target 15%): current buffer ~12% (we are slightly under target during peak).

Notes: the buffer shortfall is concentrated in EU-west where a combination of rolling OS/kernel upgrades and a transient placement-group shortage reduced available hosts for ~3 hours on 08-28. We did not hit customer account limits due to our cross-region routing fallback, but regional warm pools were temporarily depleted.

2) Regions and routing
- US-west: Stable. Continued ramp of A100 jobs from recent model onboarding. Scheduled kernel/driver patch on 2026-09-07 (maintenance window) — will notify customers with reserved capacity.
- US-east: Healthy. Autoscaler tuning reduced cold-starts by ~14% after adjusting max-burst settings.
- EU-west: Experienced degradation on 2026-08-28 during the node image rollout. Root cause: a race in the node-init script that under certain AMI images caused docker-engine to fail to start. Rollback to previous image restored capacity.
- APAC (ap-southeast): Warm pool maintained but under-provisioned for H100. Procurement and allocation for APAC H100 nodes planned in the next tranche.

Routing action items taken:
- Implemented temporary routing rule to prefer US regions for non-EU data residency workloads to preserve EU capacity for customers with residency constraints.
- Increased prefix cache retention on edge routers to reduce cross-region repeat requests during failover events.

3) Incidents and postmortem notes
- Incident: EU-west capacity dip (2026-08-28)
  - Impact: degraded scheduling for ~3 hours. No SLA violations; higher cold-start latency for some host-boot operations.
  - Root cause: node-init race leading to container runtime start failure on a subset of AMI images.
  - Mitigation: immediate rollback to prior AMI, requeued affected tasks, drained faulty hosts.
  - Action items: add additional preflight checks to node-init, increase canary percentage for future AMI rollouts to 5% (was 1%), add automated health gate that verifies container runtime before marking host healthy. Assigned to: Xiaowen Li (owner).

4) Maintenance and upgrades
- Completed: Rolling upgrade of NVIDIA driver to 535.XX on 60% of hosts (US-west and US-east). Initial telemetry shows modest improvement in p95 latency for short sequence workloads.
- In progress: Full node-image update (OS + container runtime) across remaining hosts. Expected completion: 2026-09-03.
- Planned: H100 driver/kernel compatibility test matrix scheduled 2026-09-02. This precedes the larger H100 node onboarding.

5) Dedicated / Reserved capacity customers
- Dedicated pools: stable. Two new Dedicated contracts (enterprise) signed this week; onboarding scheduled in September and will consume an estimated 18 H100-equivalent GPUs.
- Autoscaling policy templates: released v2 that supports burst capacity with soft limits and predictable overcommit to maximize utilization while protecting reserved capacity.

6) Cost and utilization workstreams
- Batching and cache improvements from Optimize team reduced token compute by ~6% on sampled workloads when enabled. Infrastructure team working with Optimize to propose default bin-pack policies by workload class.
- Spot/Preemptible strategy: evaluating a mixed-instance approach for non-latency-sensitive workloads to lower unit cost. Proof-of-concept running in US-west with ~30% cost reduction for background eval jobs.

7) Upcoming procurement and capacity planning
- H100 tranche (order placed): 96 H100 GPUs expected in deliveries across Sept-Oct (split US/EU).
- Goal: increase H100 pool to support 99th percentile latency-sensitive workloads and Dedicated customers.
- Short-term plan: reallocate 8 H100-equivalent from internal bench to customer-facing pools after compatibility tests complete.

8) Standup highlights / blockers (from daily notes)
- Blocker: QA for H100 images still has two failing test cases related to multi-GPU NVLink topology detection (owner: Miguel Torres).
- Blocker: automation to re-provision warm pool nodes after evictions needs an idempotent recovery path (owner: Liam O'Connor).
- Done: Autoscaler max-burst tuning merged to main (PR #924).

9) Action items and owners
- Xiaowen Li: implement node-init preflight checks and increase AMI canary percent (target 2026-09-04).
- Miguel Torres: finalize NVLink detection fixes and update test harness (target 2026-09-06).
- Liam O'Connor: build idempotent warm-pool reprovisioner and run a chaos test (target 2026-09-08).
- Priya Shah: finalize H100 rollout playbook and coordinate customer comms for Dedicated onboarding (target 2026-09-03).

10) Notes to stakeholders
- We are slightly under our spare capacity buffer during peak demand due to transient failures and procurement timing. Proactive mitigations (routing and warm-pool reallocation) prevented customer impact, but please expect slightly higher cold-starts during peak windows until H100 tranche arrives.
- Dedicated customers should be brought into planned maintenance windows for kernel/driver updates; product/CS will coordinate calendar invites this week.

Appendix: quick command snippets and checks (ops runbook references)
- Check pool utilization: ./infra-cli pools list --region eu-west --format short
- Drain host: ./infra-cli hosts drain --host-id <id> --reason "kernel-upgrade-fix"
- Canary AMI test: ./infra-cli images canary --ami-id <ami> --percent 5

If you want a deeper breakdown (per-customer impact, per-cluster telemetry graphs), I can attach the dashboards / export next update.

-- Priya
